name: httpserve_start

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Interface to bind on. Use `'localhost'` (or `'127.0.0.1'`) to keep the server reachable only from the same machine. Use `'0.0.0.0'` to listen on all interfaces — only do this behind a firewall or reverse proxy.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: TCP port to listen on. Any unused port; `9999` is conventional in the upstream examples. `0` lets the OS pick a free port, which the returned message names.

parameters.name: auth
parameters.description: Authentication selector. **Empty string** disables auth (development only). A value containing `':'` is parsed as `user:password` and enables [HTTP Basic auth](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7617). Any other value is treated as a single shared key the client must send in the `X-API-Key` header. There is one credential per server — no per-user accounts. Each mode accepts only its own header: a `user:password` credential only through HTTP Basic, a key only in `X-API-Key`.

returns: Confirmation string of the form `'HTTP server started on <host>:<port>'`.
description:
Start the embedded HTTP query server. The listener runs in a background thread inside the DuckDB process and runs each request on a fresh connection to the same database instance — extensions you've `LOAD`ed and databases you've `ATTACH`ed are visible to HTTP clients; temporary tables and `SET VARIABLE` values are not.

There is one global server per DuckDB process: calling `httpserve_start` while it is running raises `HTTP server is already running` — call `httpserve_stop` first. The port is bound before the function returns; if it can't be bound, the call raises `Failed to start HTTP server on <host>:<port>` and nothing is left running. Set `DUCKDB_HTTPSERVER_FOREGROUND=1` before starting DuckDB to run the server on the main thread (the SQL caller will block); set `DUCKDB_HTTPSERVER_DEBUG=1` for stdout request logging or `DUCKDB_HTTPSERVER_SYSLOG=1` to route logs to syslog; set `DUCKDB_HTTPSERVER_BASEPATH=/prefix/` to serve the endpoints under a path prefix.

The served endpoints are:

- `/` — `GET` and `POST` for SQL queries. Pass SQL in the request body, or as `?query=` / `?q=`. The response is `JSONEachRow` by default; add `?default_format=JSONCompact`, `CSV`, or `XML` to choose another shape (see ClickHouse formats — the names are borrowed from there). Failed queries return HTTP `500` with the error text.
- `/ping` — unauthenticated `GET` health check; returns `OK`.
- The browser UI (*quackplay*) is served from `/` when a request carries no query.

examples.code:
SELECT httpserve_start('localhost', 9999, 'user:pass');
-- 'HTTP server started on localhost:9999'

-- From the shell:
--   curl -X POST -d "SELECT version()" http://user:pass@localhost:9999/

SELECT httpserve_start('localhost', 9999, 'supersecretkey');

-- From the shell:
--   curl -X POST --header 'X-API-Key: supersecretkey' \
--        -d 'SELECT 42' http://localhost:9999/?default_format=JSONCompact

examples.description: No auth — only behind a private network
Bind on all interfaces — read-only DuckDB, behind a TLS-terminating proxy
examples.code:
-- Launched as: duckdb -readonly mydata.duckdb
SELECT httpserve_start('0.0.0.0', 9999, 'shared-api-key');

name: httpserve_stop
returns: Confirmation string indicating the listener has been stopped.
description:
Stop the running HTTP server thread cleanly. Pair with `httpserve_start` when you want to rebind on a different port or rotate the auth credential without restarting DuckDB.

If the DuckDB process exits, the server thread is torn down with it — calling `httpserve_stop` is not strictly required for shutdown, only for in-process restarts.
